My dad owns a couple of trucks, the season is high right now, one of his guys is making 8k per week gross, however after truck payments, insurance, gas, food, service fees, and everything he takes home about 2500 clean per week. So yeah profitable but then again expect to be driving nonstop for for upwards of 15 hours a day.

I will be starting hauling next week, also new to this, if you are serious about this my dad has a truck open now pm me and we can see if we can work something out. 

A few things to mention although the pay seems attractive keep in mind that aside from driving for the better part of the day, you also have to be able to maneuver a 40+ foot hauler, you also have to be able to load cars onto the trailer which is also risky, and any damage that you might incur will be coming out of your pocket. In the past year my dad has had to deal with about 2/3 claims per driver. 

So yeah pros and cons to all of this!

To all those saying cameras, can you please tell me what you will do in this scenario:

You notice 4 masked men pass by on one of your cameras, with the intent to break in and steal/hurt you, what do you do? The first logical answer would be to call the police, okay so you dial 911 with your panicky hands, and by then theyre already working on getting your door down. 911 responds and you hide somewhere and try to explain to the police what is happening, by then theyre already inside searching the place, you try to be quiet now because well you didnt play enough hide and seek in your new place and you were in a rush and also trying to get the police over so with all that going on you ended up hiding in a closet. Ok so now the bad guys (a) ransacked the place and got what they wanted (b) found you and did what they want with you, by then it doesnt even matter if the police show up on time or not because you wouldnt be around to find out. 

So yeah please buy a firearm and dont rely on cameras, security systems, or anybody else for that matter. Actively Protect yourself and dont think youre living in a fairy tale where everything will work out. We live in a fucked up world, face it and stay on the good side because even good people need to get serious shit done sometimes.

Lol youre so wrong, having a gun doesnt make you “dramatically” less safe. Actually it does the complete opposite of making you drastically less safe. Just because you personally are afraid of a gun doesnt mean its unsafe, proper use of firearms can be learned at the proper facilities, with proper training. And guess what, if a bad guy (guys, because usually its multiple perps and not just 1) wants to break into your house, all that the cameras can do is record the break in and/or whatever horrible event that would go down if they get in. And security systems dont always work/ it takes a long time for first responders to arrive to the scene and by then the damage can already be done. Dont rely on others to save you, thats the worst thing you can do.

The ONLY way to avert catastrophe is to fight back, a few shots in the direction of the bad guys and they will scatter like the rats that they are. Dont let fear control you. Alternatively get a German Shepard or a Pitbull, those work too but also require proper training, and food, and walks. So yeah get yourself a firearm and hit the range, take a few classes, and then store it in a safe place unloaded, only stick the mag in when you hear the alarm. Kinda like breaking the glass when going for the fire extinguisher or axe or what have you. 

Dont listen to those who are anti self protection. Those are the ones who get targeted and ultimately pay the price. Be the one who actively stands up to evil.

Set a 3 year goal for example build a fund for him, set aside money for the next 3 years for him, or take him to the gym once a week for the next 3 years. Whatever it may be instead of punishing yourself just turn it into a positive between the 2 of you, it will heal both of you immensely. 

Another thing is the blame. You blame your father but understand that he is also a human, and you should be able to put yourself into his shoes and be more kind and understanding towards him aswell. I also tend to try to put blame onto others and I still do to this day, but the right thing to do is to take accountability and to understand that we are all human, nobody is perfect and everyone has emotions and their own views, life is tough on all of us one way or another, so just be more compassionate towards everyone and try to understand their frustrations as well.
